answer:
Assert it. But assert it as an event that both men attach to, not as a property running from one fiddler to the other -- and keep the forty sessions as well, because neither level substitutes for the other.

1) A literal direct link is not available. `connect E39 E39` returns nothing but L54 is same as; `connect E21 E21` returns exactly one declared person-to-person property, P152 has parent. That gap is deliberate, not an oversight: Issue 256 (Done, Heraklion Oct 2017) closed with the finding that social relations of the prosopographical kind go beyond the scope of CRMBase, deferring them to a possible 'CRMsoc' that has still not delivered them. The ULAN 'student of / teacher of' pair is the very example on the table when that was decided (t0834), and Christian-Emil Ore had already noted for the analogous curator case that there is effectively no direct actor-to-actor link in the model (t0337). Minimality means the archive should not mint a local 'taught' property and present it as CRM.

2) Chaining the forty sessions will not produce the relationship either. What a tape supports is that both men were present and playing: P11 had participant, whose scope note says in as many words that participation does not imply any causal relationship. Forty instances of a non-causal relation still yield no causal one. And the CRM's shortcut machinery only ever runs long-path to summary-link when a shortcut property is *declared* for that specific path (P52 over E8, P43 over E16, P152 over E67 Birth); the spec's Shortcuts section states the entailment as one-way, and Ore's FOL homework records the SIG policy that every CRM shortcut is a 'weak' one, i.e. only the long path implies the short (t1268). No shortcut is declared for tuition, so the chain is inert: a query for 'who taught whom' returns nothing. With the Open World and monotonicity commitments of the model, what is not asserted is simply not known. 'Only inferable' here means 'absent'.

3) The CRM's own construct for a relationship between two actors is a shared, typed activity. Create one instance of E7 Activity for the three-year course of instruction: P4 has time-span the three years; P14 carried out by both fiddlers, using P14's .1 qualifier (range E55 Type) to distinguish the roles teacher and learner (the ternary form P14(x,y,z) is declared in the spec's logical expressions); P2 has type and/or P21 had general purpose an E55 Type from a folk-life vocabulary ('oral transmission of repertoire', 'tuition'); P32 used general technique an E55 Type ('learning by ear', 'imitation'). Then P9 consists of the forty session activities, each an E7 Activity with its own P4 has time-span taken from the tape date, and each with the same two participants. This is precisely the 'activity-mediated relationship' Martin Doerr floated in t0834 for relations that are neither kinship nor group membership, and the same remedy Stephen Stead recommended for P109 in t0337 -- E7 Activity plus an E55 Type rather than a new class or a new bare property. Optionally, P134 continued can record that the grandnephew's own later fiddling continued his granduncle's; P134 demands 'coherence of intentions and outcomes' and is declared asymmetric and non-transitive, which is a fair reading of carrying on a repertoire, but it is a separate claim from the tuition and should not be substituted for it.

The summary activity is what the catalogue indexes on; the forty parts carry the dates and the evidence. Keep both, because the shortcut discipline is exactly the statement that a summary link carries strictly less than the path it summarises.

Evidence side, kept minimal because that is all the tapes warrant: each minicassette is an E22 Human-Made Object; P128 carries the recording; the recording is an E31 Document (its scope note explicitly admits audiograms) and P70 documents its session. Nothing on a tape says 'lesson'.

Provenance of the assertion. Since the teaching relationship is nowhere on the record -- unlabelled tapes, no lesson plan, no tune list -- the catalogue should say where it came from rather than present it as observed. If it comes from the donating family, that is CRMinf's I7 Belief Adoption: P14 carried out by the archive, P2 has type 'Pers.Comm' (a convention I7's own scope note gives for personal communication), J2 concluded that an I2 Belief whose propositions are the tuition activity and its roles. If instead the archive reads the pattern off the tapes (play-until-reproduced), the sibling construct I5 Inference Making with J1 used as premise is the right one. This layer is an addition, not a substitute: the Shortcuts section notes that E13 Attribute Assignment and its properties do not form a long path over the property instance assigned, and the same holds of the argumentation classes -- reifying an assertion does not assert it. The E7 tuition activity still has to be stated.

Limits worth writing into the catalogue record. The transmitted repertoire cannot be documented at item level from what survives. LRMoo's F31 Performance would be the correct class for the individual tune performances inside a session, and its scope note even gives the pattern (an E7 Activity consisting of F31 Performances via P9), but F31 requires each performance to be associated with a single identified F1 Work, and the tapes are unlabelled with no tune list -- so F31 is unusable until someone identifies tunes by listening. E29 Design or Procedure is likewise unavailable: it comprises documented plans, and none survives; that is why the method must be P32 used general technique to an E55 Type rather than P33 used specific technique to an E29. And note the kinship is in the same position as the tuition: P152 has parent is declared not transitive, so 'granduncle' is not a CRM primitive either and has to be composed from elementary parenthood links -- Doerr's line in t0834 that derived kinship claims are treated as fraud unless justified by elementary ones is the same discipline.

Finally, the honest scope caveat: there is no 'transfer of knowledge' class in the CRM. Issue 527 Modelling provenance of Intangible Heritage is still Open, with the SIG recording at its 53rd meeting that the construct in question cannot be defined through the CRM at that point, and Issue 648 (shortcutting knowledge/belief sharing) is Open with no archive debate at all. So the answer above is the licensed workaround -- an intentional, typed, part-decomposed activity plus a provenanced belief -- not a purpose-built construct. If the archive wants a genuine 'oral transmission' class it will have to declare it as a local extension of E7 Activity and say so, which is also what the SIG advised for the analogous curator gap.

rejected_alternatives.option: A new direct actor-to-actor property (a local 'taught' / 'learned from' between two instances of E21 Person)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: `connect E39 E39` yields only L54 is same as, and Issue 256 was closed on the finding that prosopographical social relations go beyond the scope of CRMBase, deferred to a possible CRMsoc that has not delivered them. Minimality means a locally minted property must be declared as an extension and labelled as such, not passed off as CRM.

rejected_alternatives.option: Leaving the relationship to be inferred from the forty co-participation records (P11 / P14 chains)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: P11's scope note states that participation does not imply any causal relationship, and the CRM only infers a summary link from a long path where a shortcut property is declared for that path -- all CRM shortcuts being 'weak', i.e. long-path-implies-short only (t1268). No shortcut is declared for tuition, so the chain yields nothing queryable; under the Open World assumption the claim would simply be absent from the knowledge base.

rejected_alternatives.option: P152 has parent as a template to imitate
rejected_alternatives.why_not: P152 is a declared shortcut whose full path is E21 - P98i was born - E67 Birth - P96/P97 - E21, and it is declared non-transitive precisely so that derived relations are not treated as primitives. There is no analogous declared event path for tuition, and an implementer cannot confer shortcut semantics on a property locally.

rejected_alternatives.option: E74 Group holding the pair (the SIG's older habit of modelling person-to-person relations as groups)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E74 requires a unifying relationship such that the members act collectively or in a similar way; a teacher and a pupil need not act as one unit. Ore says exactly this about the ULAN student/teacher case in t0834, and no group-based construct was adopted.

rejected_alternatives.option: LRMoo F31 Performance for the sessions or the tunes within them
rejected_alternatives.why_not: F31 requires each performance to be associated with a single identified instance of F1 Work. The tapes are unlabelled and no tune list survives, so the works are not identified; F31 becomes usable only after musicological identification from the audio.

rejected_alternatives.option: E29 Design or Procedure for the teaching method or curriculum
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E29 comprises documented plans, and the case states that no lesson plan or tune list survives. This also rules out P33 used specific technique, which ranges on E29; the method has to stay an E55 Type reached by P32 used general technique.

rejected_alternatives.option: E4 Period for the three-year run of sessions
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E4 would hold the sessions together temporally but drops the intentionality, and intentionality is the whole content of the teaching claim. E7 Activity is the narrower correct class and inherits P9 consists of from E4 anyway (confirmed by `connect E7 E7`).

rejected_alternatives.option: E10 Transfer of Custody or E8 Acquisition by analogy, as a 'transfer of knowledge'
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Both are about physical things and legal title or physical responsibility (P30/P24 range on E18 / physical things); nothing is handed over here. The CRM has no knowledge-transfer class -- Issue 527 is still Open on exactly that gap.

rejected_alternatives.option: Recording the claim only as an E13 Attribute Assignment or an I7/I5 argumentation node, without asserting the tuition activity
rejected_alternatives.why_not: The Shortcuts section states that E13 and its properties do not form a long path over the property instance assigned; reifying an assertion does not assert it. The provenance layer is additive -- the E7 tuition activity must be present in its own right.

siblings_considered.why_not: E63 Beginning of Existence and E64 End of Existence are E7's only siblings under E5, so neither is a strong rival; E63 is the closer of the two, because one could try to model the grandnephew acquiring a repertoire as the coming-into-existence of that repertoire. It fails on two counts: E63 needs P92 brought into existence an identifiable E77 Persistent Item, and no tune list survives to identify the repertoire; and E63 carries no intentionality, whereas 'intentionally carried out by instances of E39 Actor' is exactly the feature of E7 that makes the teaching claim sayable.

E74 Group is E21's only sibling under E39, and modelling the pair as a group was the SIG's older answer to person-to-person relations. It is wrong here: E74 requires a unifying relationship such that members act collectively or similarly, and Ore argues in t0834 that a student and a teacher need not be seen as members of one group. The two fiddlers are individually identified real persons, which is what E21 comprises.

E89 Propositional Object comprises things that are or represent sets of propositions about real or imaginary things. 'Tuition by ear' is a term from a controlled vocabulary used to characterise an event, not a proposition that can be true or false -- which is exactly the boundary E55's scope note draws, and its own examples include types for instances of E5 Event ('wedding, earthquake, skirmish').

E78 Curated Holding legitimately describes the accessioned set of forty tapes as an aggregation curated for a purpose, and the archive may well want it. It cannot replace E22 at the level the argument needs: each individual tape is a bounded object with its own date and its own single recording, so each must be the domain of its own P128 carries. E78 would flatten the per-session evidence the question turns on.

E29 Design or Procedure, a sibling of E31 under E73, is the tempting class for 'how the teaching was done', but it comprises *documented* plans and the case says no lesson plan or tune list survives. E31 is the right sibling because its scope note explicitly covers propositions expressed as audiograms, which is what a field recording of a session is.

I5 Inference Making, a sibling under I1 Argumentation, is for conclusions drawn from premises by some inference logic. The teaching relationship does not come off the tapes by inference -- the tapes are unlabelled and show only co-performance -- it comes from the donating family, and I7 Belief Adoption is the construct grounded in trust in a source rather than rule application, with its scope note supplying the P2 has type 'Pers.Comm' convention for personal communication. If the archive does derive the claim from the audio, I5 is the correct class instead.

E4 Period, a sibling of I2 under E2 Temporal Entity, comprises sets of coherent phenomena or cultural manifestations in spacetime. The archive's holding-true of the tuition proposition is not a phenomenon located in space; I2 Belief is defined as the period over which an actor holds a proposition set to a belief value, which is what needs recording.

notes: Three things the tools made awkward. (1) `docs` truncates every hit to roughly 300 characters, so the decisive passages -- the Shortcuts section with its shortcut / inverse shortcut / strong shortcut definitions, and the Minimality criteria -- were only readable after discovering the undocumented `--json` flag, which prints the full chunk text and, more importantly, the chunk_id (e.g. crm732#s0032, crm732#P11, issue256#outcome) that `quote` needs. `quote` rejects concept identifiers and section paths outright, so without --json there is no way to verify a quotation from the reference document at all. That is worth fixing; it is the difference between citing the spec and paraphrasing it. (2) `concept` prints no siblings block for family-model classes: I1 Argumentation lists I5, I7, I15, I16, E13 and S27 as its subclasses, so I7's siblings are recoverable, but only by looking up the parent by hand. (3) I7 Belief Adoption's scope note names I12 Adopted belief as the class of its conclusion, but `concept I12` reports 'No such concept', so I could not inspect or cite it and stated the conclusion at the I2 Belief level instead, which is J2's declared range. Two substantive gaps in the model itself, not the tools: there is no knowledge-transfer or oral-transmission class anywhere in CRMbase or the indexed family models (Issue 527 Open, Issue 648 Open with no archive debate recorded), and the 58th meeting minutes note an attempt to model intangible cultural heritage for Iranian traditional music but the section is one line of discussion points with no construct in it, so it settled nothing for this case.
